arxiv-2105-07195.title: Energy and Randić energy of special graphs
arxiv-2105-07195.creator: Jahfar T K, Chithra A V
arxiv-2105-07195.description: Abstract In this paper, we determine the Randić energy of the m m -splitting graph, the m m -shadow graph and the m m -duplicate graph of a given graph, m m being an arbitrary integer. Our results allow the construction of an infinite sequence of graphs having the same Randić energy.

arxiv-2203-04775.title: Software Training in High Energy Physics
arxiv-2203-04775.creator: Michel H. Villanueva 1, Sudhir Malik 2, Meirin Oan Evans 3
arxiv-2203-04775.description: Abstract Among the upgrades in current high energy physics (HEP) experiments and the new facilities coming online, solving software challenges has become integral for the success of the collaborations, The demand for human resources highly-skilled in both HEP and software domains is increasing.

arxiv-2205-12330.title: Non-invasive estimation of left ventricle elastance using a multi-compartment lumped parameter model and gradient-based optimization with forward-mode automatic differentiation Journal: Computers in Biology and Medicine
arxiv-2205-12330.creator: Ryno Laubscher and Johan van der Merwe, Jacques Liebenberg and Philip Herbst
arxiv-2205-12330.description: Abstract Accurate estimates of left ventricle elastances based on non-invasive measurements are required for clinical decision-making during treatment of valvular diseases. The present study proposes a parameter discovery approach based on a lumped parameter model of the cardiovascular system in conjunction with optimization and non-invasive, clinical input measurements to approximate important cardiac parameters, including left ventricle elastances.

arxiv-2205-13786.title: Modeling the effectiveness of radiation shielding materials for astronaut protection on Mars
arxiv-2205-13786.creator: Dionysios Gakis, Dimitra Atri
arxiv-2205-13786.description: Abstract The surface of Mars is bombarded by energetic charged particles of solar and cosmic origin with little shielding compared to Earth. As space agencies are planning for crewed missions to the red planet, a major concern is the impact of ionizing radiation on astronaut health.

arxiv-2304-07563.title: Error estimates of invariant-preserving difference schemes for the rotation-two-component Camassa–Holm system with small energy Thanks: Qifeng Zhang was supported by Zhejiang Provincial Natural Science Foundation of China (Grant No. LZ23A010007). Zhimin Zhang was supported by the National Natural Sc
arxiv-2304-07563.creator: Qifeng Zhang, Jiyuan Zhang, Zhimin Zhang
arxiv-2304-07563.description: Abstract A rotation-two-component Camassa-Holm (R2CH) system was proposed recently to describe the motion of shallow water waves under the influence of gravity. This is a highly nonlinear and strongly coupled system of partial differential equations. A crucial issue in designing numerical schemes is to preserve invariants as many as possible at the discrete level.

Open Radio Access Networks (O-RAN) are expected to revolutionize the telecommunications industry with benefits like cost reduction, vendor diversity, and improved network performance through AI optimization.

arxiv-2504-17674.title: Energy Considerations of Large Language Model Inference and Efficiency Optimizations
arxiv-2504-17674.creator: Jared Fernandez, Clara Na, Vashisth Tiwari, Yonatan Bisk, Sasha Luccioni, Emma Strubell
arxiv-2504-17674.description: Abstract As large language models (LLMs) scale in size and adoption, their computational and environmental costs continue to rise. Prior benchmarking efforts have primarily focused on latency reduction in idealized settings, often overlooking the diverse real-world inference workloads that shape energy use.

arxiv-2505-24004.title: Redefining Research Crowdsourcing: Incorporating Human Feedback with LLM-Powered Digital Twins Conference: Extended Abstracts of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems; April 26-May 1, 2025; Yokohama, Japan Extended Abstracts of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Syst

arxiv-2505-24004.description: Abstract . Crowd work platforms like Amazon Mechanical Turk and Prolific are vital for research, yet workers’ growing use of generative AI tools poses challenges. Researchers face compromised data validity as AI responses replace authentic human behavior, while workers risk diminished roles as AI automates tasks.

arxiv-2511-11843.title: TD-Orch: Scalable Load-Balancing for Distributed Systems with Applications to Graph Processing Conference: ACM SIGPLAN Annual Symposium on Principles and Practice of Parallel Programming; January 31–February 04, 2026; Sydney, Australia
arxiv-2511-11843.creator: Yiwei Zhao, Qiushi Lin, Hongbo Kang, Guy E. Blelloch, Laxman Dhulipala, Charles McGuffey, Phillip B. Gibbons
arxiv-2511-11843.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yiwei Zhao, Qiushi Lin, Hongbo Kang, Guy E. Blelloch, Laxman Dhulipala, Charles McGuffey, Phillip B. Gibbons. In this paper, we highlight a task-data orchestration abstraction that supports a range of distributed applications, including graph processing and key-value stores. Given a batch of tasks each requesting one or more data items, where both tasks and data are distributed across multiple machines, each task must get co-located with its target data (by moving tasks and/or data) and executed.

arxiv-2512-04756.title: Secret Key Generation On Aerial Rician Fading Channels Against A Curious Receiver
arxiv-2512-04756.creator: Mattia Piana, Stefano Tomasin
arxiv-2512-04756.description: Abstract Secret key generation at the physical layer is expected to be a fundamental enabler for next-generation networks. We consider a network where the user equipment is a drone and propose a novel secret key generation solution when the eavesdropper is another node belonging to the network (curious device). We exploit drone mobility over realistic Rician fading channels.

arxiv-2601-18493.title: DisasterInsight: A Multimodal Benchmark for Function-Aware and Grounded Disaster Assessment
arxiv-2601-18493.creator: Sara Tehrani, Yonghao Xu, Leif Haglund, Amanda Berg, Michael Felsberg
arxiv-2601-18493.description: Abstract Timely interpretation of satellite imagery is critical for disaster response, yet existing vision–language benchmarks for remote sensing largely focus on coarse labels and image-level recognition, overlooking the functional understanding and instruction robustness required in real humanitarian workflows. We introduce DisasterInsight, a multimodal benchmark designed to evaluate vision–language models (VLMs) on realistic disaster analysis tasks.

pmc-10713951.creator: Federica Foglietta, Loredana Serpe, Roberto Canaparo
pmc-10713951.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Reactive species refers to a group of chemicals, mainly reactive oxygen species (ROS) and reactive nitrogen species (RNS), that are naturally formed by cells as a byproduct of cell metabolism and regulated by various internal and external factors. Due to their highly chemical reactivity, ROS play a crucial role in physiological and pathological processes which is why studies on ROS regulation for disease treatment show attracted increasing interest.

pmc-11517963.title: Growth and challenges in biomedical scientific publishing: the phenomenon of mega-journals
pmc-11517963.creator: A M Pezzullo, S Boccia
pmc-11517963.description: The landscape of academic scientific publishing has seen relentless growth, with the number of articles published and indexed on Web of Science exceeding three million in 2023 alone. This increase in both the number of publications and authors has significantly impacted scientific research, enhancing our collective knowledge.

pmc-11657063.title: Pesticides as an overlooked exposomic association in allergic asthma exacerbations: A nationwide database study
pmc-11657063.creator: Joana Vitte, Leila Bouazzi, Coralie Barbe, Bach‐Nga Pham, Stéphane Sanchez
pmc-11657063.description: idered a minor exposomic risk. 1 , 2 , 3 Pesticides share the One Health pathophysiology of exposome‐related diseases: leaky barrier due to epithelial lesions and inflammation driven by epithelium‐derived alarmins. Leaky barriers allow further penetration of noxious molecules while the vicious circle of chronic inflammation, most often type 2‐skewed, fosters and exacerbates adaptive allergic responses to common airborne allergens.

pmc-12428675.title: An Integrated System Combining Filter-Assisted Sample Preparation and Colorimetric Biosensing for Rapid Pathogen Detection in Complex Food Matrices
pmc-12428675.creator: Jihae Lee, Youngsang You, Yi Xu
pmc-12428675.description: Climate change increases microbial contamination risks in food, highlighting the need for real-time biosensors. However, food residues often interfere with detection signals, limiting the direct application. An integrated system of filter-assisted sample preparation (FASP) and an immunoassay-based colorimetric biosensor offers the rapid and simple on-site detection of foodborne pathogens in complex food matrices.

pmc-12741433.title: Garré’s Chronic Sclerosing Osteomyelitis: An Overview of Clinical and Radiologic Features
pmc-12741433.creator: Mohamed Fadil, Ayman Farouki, Rachida Saouab, Hassan En-nouali, Jamal El Fenni, Zakariya Toufga
pmc-12741433.description: Garré's chronic sclerosing osteomyelitis is a rare, nonsuppurative form of chronic osteomyelitis, typically seen in children and adolescents, and characterized by periosteal bone proliferation. This case report presents an unusual manifestation in a 20-year-old male with recurrent swelling of the left cheek and trismus, in whom imaging and clinical evolution supported the diagnosis.

pmc-13355482.title: Taurochenodeoxycholic acid alleviates MPP+/MPTP-induced neurotoxicity in vitro and in vivo by suppressing ferroptosis via TGR5/cGAS/STING signaling pathway
pmc-13355482.creator: Lupeng Wang, Ying Ni, Xuefang Wang, Yanni Ma, Yanli Chang, Ling Chen, Liqin Yu, Zhiyong He, Feifei Li
pmc-13355482.description: Parkinson's disease (PD) is characterized by progressive loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra, with ferroptosis emerging as critical pathogenic mechanisms. Recent evidence suggests that STING activation can induce neuronal ferroptosis through autophagic degradation of GPX4. Taurochenodeoxycholic acid (TCDCA), a naturally occurring bile acid, has demonstrated neuroprotective properties through activation of Takeda G protein-coupled receptor 5 (TGR5).
